Class PeriodHoldingsLoader

java.lang.Object
grafioschtrader.reports.PeriodHoldingsLoader
@Component public class PeriodHoldingsLoader extends Object
Loads the daily holdings of a tenant or portfolio for the period performance report, reading the days the task HOLD_DAILY_TOTAL_UPDATE has already stored from hold_daily_total and only the remaining days through the period holdings query.

The stored rows are copies of that query, so a stored day and a computed day are the same. Reading them is what makes the report fast: over twenty years the query took 7 s for a tenant, the stored rows 0.1 s. A day is taken from the table only when it is known to be current, that is

  • on or after the first stored day of the scope. The task starts at the zero base, the live query also returns the cash-only days before it;
  • before the marker recalc_from_date of the tenant, which bookings lower at once;
  • before the earliest day whose price was created or changed since the last run of the task. Such a price, for example a back-filled gap, only lowers the marker on the next run, and until then the stored rows of that day and the following ones are outdated or missing.

A tenant the task has never computed has no marker; all its days come from the query. The periodic prices of historyquote_period carry no timestamp, so a change of one is noticed by neither the task nor this loader.

Everything is read in one read-only transaction, so the marker and the rows belong to the same snapshot even when the task rewrites the rows at the same moment.

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public List<IPeriodHolding> load(Integer idTenant, Integer idPortfolio, LocalDate dateFrom, LocalDate dateTo)
      The daily holdings of a tenant or of one of its portfolios between two days, exactly as the period holdings query returns them for that range.
      Parameters:
      idTenant - the tenant; for a portfolio the tenant it belongs to
      idPortfolio - the portfolio, or null for the total of the tenant
      dateFrom - the first day, inclusive
      dateTo - the last day, inclusive
      Returns:
      the days in ascending order
